meta.description: Batch effect correction for CRISPR screens covering ComBat empirical-Bayes, RUV, SVA, control-sgRNA normalization, and the model-based alternative of including batch as a covariate in MAGeCK MLE or Chronos, plus diagnosis, decision-tree guidance, and when correction harms biology.

scientific_integrity.detail: All cited references (Johnson 2007 Biostatistics, Leek 2012 Bioinformatics, Risso 2014 Nat Biotechnol, Pacini 2021 Nat Commun, Vinceti 2024 Genome Biol) remain real, correctly attributed papers, unchanged by the fix. No fabricated statistics, DOIs, or results in any of the 7 post-fix outputs; all quantitative results (AUCs, betas, NaN counts, correlations) trace to real HAP1 TKOv3 data or clearly-labeled synthetic data with disclosed ground truth, re-verified this round.

practice_boundaries.detail: Pure computational-biology screen analysis; no diagnostic, prescriptive, or clinical claims about individuals anywhere in scope, before or after the fix.

methodological_ground.detail: Confounding, covariate modeling, and empirical-Bayes assumptions remain handled correctly (Input 3). The auditor's own investigation (Input 5) found the within-batch-constant filter is methodologically broader than strictly necessary -- it excludes some guides that were never at risk of the NaN corruption it targets -- but this is a completeness gap, not a methodological fallacy: it never produces a wrong answer, only a conservatively unconnected one for a small, always-reported subset.

code_usability.detail: All three previously-crashing/silently-corrupting patterns now run cleanly: combat_correct() with a covariate on 71,090 real guides (Input 1), RUVg's SeqExpressionSet dispatch (Input 2), and MAGeCK MLE with the newly-documented --permutation-round flag (Input 4, confirmed present in `mageck mle --help`). The one input designed to trigger a failure (Input 7, forcing ComBat on batch-free data) now fails via a clear, intentional ValueError instead of silently returning a 568,720/568,720-NaN matrix with exit code 0 -- the underlying pycombat call was independently re-confirmed to still do that; the wrapper is what changed.

functional_suitability.note: Both P1 code patterns (combat_correct() covariate usage, RUV cIdx) now run cleanly verbatim on real data (Inputs 1, 2). Docked 1 pt: the within-batch-constant filter is broader than the actual NaN-causing condition (found by reading pycombat's source and reproducing both the filter's trigger and the true trigger separately in Input 5), unnecessarily leaving some correctable guides -- 294/71,090 on real HAP1 data including 14 essential-gene guides -- permanently batch-confounded rather than corrected.

reliability.note: combat_correct() now raises an actionable ValueError instead of silently returning all-NaN (Input 7, regression-verified), and the pre-fit filter independently prevents a second, milder failure mode the post-hoc check alone would miss (Input 5 Part 5: a numerically-fragile variant that collapses affected genes to a wrong-but-finite constant instead of NaN). Docked 2 pts: dropped/uncorrected guides are only reported as a printed count, never returned to the caller as an identifiable list, which blocks automated follow-up.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md remains dense but relevant (grew modestly for the fix's docstring and two new paragraphs/sections, no unrelated bloat); usage-guide.md unchanged in weight.

agent_usability.note: Both previously-crashing 'Critical' patterns now work exactly as documented, out of the box, on first try (Inputs 1, 2). Docked 1 pt: using combat_correct() safely still requires understanding the drop-and-report nuance, which the Validation Checklist doesn't call out.

human_usability.note: Failures now surface as a clear, actionable ValueError message instead of a raw pycombat/RUVSeq traceback (Inputs 2, 7). Docked 1 pt: the verbose drop-count print is easy to miss in agent transcripts, and there is no structured way to retrieve which specific guides were affected.

security.note: The new pre-fit filter and post-hoc NaN/Inf guard are effective validation of the DATA passing through combat_correct(). Docked 1 pt: the function's own arguments (batch_vector, condition_vector, mod) still have no type/shape validation, unchanged from pre-fix.

maintainability.note: Evidence of real testing is now visible directly in the docstring, which cites a measured result ('6 such guides out of 2,000 produced an all-NaN matrix') -- the auditor independently reproduced this class of failure and confirmed the fix eliminates it (Input 5). Docked 1 pt: no automated smoke test ships with the Skill; the evidence lives only in prose.

agent_specific.note: The new 'Related but out of scope' section closes the pre-fix scope-boundary gap: Input 6's escape-hatch assertion, which FAILed pre-fix, now PASSes. Docked 1 pt: the Common Errors table and Validation Checklist still don't mention the within-batch-constant drop mechanism or that it can leave a small fraction of guides intentionally uncorrected.

key_strengths: All three pre-fix P1 code-crash/silent-corruption bugs are genuinely fixed and independently regression-tested: combat_correct() with a covariate now runs cleanly on 71,090 real guides (Input 1), RUVg's cIdx fix eliminates the S4 dispatch error while the old pattern was re-confirmed to still fail (Input 2), and forcing ComBat on batch-free data now raises an actionable ValueError instead of silently returning a 100%-NaN matrix -- the underlying pycombat call was independently re-verified to still do that; the fix is entirely, correctly, in the wrapper (Input 7).

The fix log's own most novel, previously-untested claim ('6 zero-within-batch guides out of 2,000 produced an all-NaN matrix') is real: independently reproduced under controlled conditions (Input 5/5b), and the auditor's investigation shows the shipped two-layer design (pre-filter + post-hoc check) is necessary, not redundant -- the post-hoc NaN check alone would miss a milder, numerically-fragile manifestation the auditor also reproduced (Input 5 Part 5).

MAGeCK MLE's batch-covariate betas are confirmed deterministic under the newly-documented --permutation-round flag: identical top essential genes and AUC (0.9685) to the pre-fix audit despite the different permutation setting, and the flag itself was confirmed to be a real, recognized mageck 0.5.9.5 option, not a plausible-looking invention (Input 4).

The new 'Related but out of scope' section closes the pre-fix audit's scope-boundary gap cleanly and concisely (Input 6): an agent asked about non-CRISPR batch correction can now cite an explicit answer instead of inferring the boundary from the frontmatter alone.

recommendations.title: Within-batch-constant filter over-excludes guides that were never actually at risk
recommendations.problem: combat_correct()'s per-batch std>0 filter flags a guide if it is constant within ANY single batch, but the actual NaN-causing condition (confirmed by reading pycombat's source and testing both conditions separately) requires zero POOLED variance across ALL batches combined. Guides that are constant in one batch but ordinarily noisy in another are safe to correct, yet are dropped anyway -- 294/71,090 on real HAP1 data (Input 1, including 14 CEGv2 essential-gene guides) and 6/6 in a controlled comparison (Input 5 Part 4).
recommendations.root_cause: The filter checks each batch's variance independently (an easy, cheap per-batch check) rather than the pooled-across-all-batches variance that pycombat's compute_prior() actually divides by.
recommendations.fix: Replace the per-batch std>0 check with a pooled-residual check (e.g. regress out batch+mod via the same design matrix pycombat uses internally, or a simpler proxy: flag a guide only if ALL of its batches are individually constant, not just one), so guides with real information in at least one noisy batch are still corrected.

recommendations.title: Dropped/uncorrected guides are reported only as a count, not returned to the caller
recommendations.problem: combat_correct() prints '<N> features are constant within a batch' but returns a single DataFrame with no column or accompanying mask indicating which specific rows were left uncorrected, so a downstream pipeline cannot selectively re-examine, re-normalize, or exclude them from hit-calling without re-deriving the same per-batch std check itself.
recommendations.root_cause: The `usable` boolean mask computed inside the function is local and discarded after use; only its count is surfaced via print().
recommendations.fix: Return a tuple (or attach a boolean Series as a `.attrs['uncorrected_features']`) so the caller can identify and act on the dropped guides directly, e.g. flag them in the final hit-calling report rather than silently including them alongside genuinely-corrected values.

recommendations.title: The 'all-NaN' failure mode is framed as reliable; it is floating-point fragile
recommendations.problem: combat_correct()'s docstring and the SKILL.md prose describe the danger as producing NaNs 'with no exception and exit code 0.' Testing the identical zero-pooled-variance construction against a dataset with a realistic per-batch baseline shift instead of a uniform one showed it can instead silently collapse the affected genes to a wrong-but-finite constant value -- no NaN at all -- depending on floating-point round-off in the underlying linear-algebra solve.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix log's own measurement ('6/2,000 -> all-NaN') was taken under one specific data shape; the failure's exact numerical manifestation was not characterized as data-shape-dependent.
recommendations.fix: Reframe the docstring/prose to say the pre-fit filter, not the post-hoc NaN check, is what reliably prevents this class of failure (both the NaN and the degenerate-constant manifestations) -- so a future editor doesn't remove the filter under the assumption the NaN check alone is sufficient.
